name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  September 8, 2009

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board
of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 5:04
p.m., on September 8, 2009 at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on September 4, 2009, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

For Mayor Pro Tem MacLean’s audio teleconference location, a complete copy of the Agenda
was posted by 5:00 p.m. on September 5, 2009, at the Courtyard Marriott, 2650 S. Beulah, Room
111, Flagstaff, Arizona 86001.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley (arrived at 5:07 p.m.)
  Council Member Ledesma
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean (arrived at 6:00 p.m. from teleconferencing location)
  Mayor Ury

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Ury

INVOCATION: Council Member Schlicht

CLOSED SESSION

City Council Minutes  1  September 8, 2009
 CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel -- Initiation of Litigation. Pursuant to Subdivision
  (c) of Government Code Section 54956.9. Two (2) Cases Under Consideration.

CS2. Conference with the City’s Real Property Negotiator (City Manager/Executive
  Director Dennis Wilberg, City Attorney William Curley, and Director of Public
  Services Keith Rattay) Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.8 Concerning
  Real Property (4.9 acre slope) Located on the Eastside of Marguerite Parkway,
  between Vista Del Lago and Ameno Streets in the City of Mission Viejo. The
  Negotiating Parties Are the City of Mission Viejo and the Mallorca Homeowners
  Association. Under Negotiation Will Be the Price and Terms of Payment for the
  Property Interest to Be Acquired. Final Action, if any, on This Matter will be Taken
  in Public Session at a Future Council Meeting Following Public Comments.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

  At the hour of 5:10 p.m., Mayor Ury recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
  Council reconvened at 6:07 p.m. with all five City Council Members present. Mayor Pro
  Tem MacLean began participating in the meeting via audio teleconference from
  Flagstaff, Arizona.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

  City Attorney Bill Curley announced that for Closed Session Item CS1, there were two
  matters considered. For the first matter, there was no action taken and therefore nothing
  to report. For the second matter, the City Council authorized commencement of a CEQA
  action against the Saddleback Valley Unified School District relating to the closure of
  O’Neill School. That action will commence immediately. The vote on this item was 3-1-
  1 with Council Member Schlicht opposing commencement of the litigation until she gets
  further information (Mayor Pro Tem MacLean did not participate in the Closed Session
  conference and did not vote).

  For CS2, City Attorney Curley announced that the Council terminated the discussion and
  directed staff to place an item on the next open session agenda to obtain policy direction
  regarding the acquisition of the subject slope land.

Mayor Ury announced that the meetings of the City Council, Community Development Agency,
Community Development Financing Authority, Public Improvement Corporation, and the
Library Board of Trustees would be conducted with Mayor Pro Tem MacLean participating
through audio teleconferencing as authorized by Government Code Section 54953 and that

City Council Minutes  2  September 8, 2009
 Mayor Pro Tem MacLean would be participating from the Courtyard Marriott, 2650 S. Beulah,
Room 111, Flagstaff, Arizona.

City Clerk Hamman requested that Mayor Ury take all votes during this teleconferenced meeting
by roll call for audio clarity.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Recognize Waste Management for their $4,211.05 Donation to the Friends of the
  Mission Viejo Library

  Mayor Ury and Director of Library Services Valerie Maginnis received the donation
  check from Michelle Clark, Community Relations Manager for Waste Management.
  Mayor Ury presented a Certificate of Appreciation to Ms. Clark.

P3.  Recognize the 10th Anniversary of Passport Services at the Mission Viejo Library

  Mayor Ury presented the Proclamation to Valerie Maginnis, Director of Library Services.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Norbert Kaufmann, M.V.: expressed outrage that $250,000 of taxpayer money may be
  spent on a recall election just a few months before the general election in November.

  City Attorney Bill Curley described the recall process and confirmed that recall
  proceedings occur outside of the City Council’s control.

  Catherine Jasper, M.V.: expressed concern with the ongoing construction at 26992 La
  Paja Lane and stated that the neighbors were promised a timeline in July, yet they have
  never seen one.

  Nancy Cho, Chairperson of the Mission Viejo Heritage Committee, M.V.: thanked the
  City Council for their support and announced that the Heritage Committee will be selling
  Mission Viejo playing cards at the Readers’ Festival on Saturday.

  Jan MacDonald, M.V.: thanked the City Council and staff for making Mission Viejo
  paradise in her family’s eyes.

  The following spoke in support of a Dog Park in Mission Viejo: Susan Sellers, M.V.;
  Corissa Sellers, M.V.; Joey Sellers, M.V.; Sarah Grimberg, M.V.; Diane Shows Wiley,
  M.V.

City Council Minutes  3  September 8, 2009
   The following presented written comments in favor of a dog park in Mission Viejo:
  Stephanie Colby, M.V.; S. Hepler, M.V.; A Hepler, M.V.; Suzi Scallon, M.V.; Sarah
  Grimberg, M.V.; Susan Sellers, M.V.; and Scott Palmer, M.V.

  Joe Holtzman, M.V.: announced that the Mission Viejo Environmental Association is in
  the process of displaying a drought-tolerant display area on the corner of Vantella and
  Marguerite. He further announced that he has reviewed the Mallorca Condominium
  Association Board Meeting Minutes for the past year and not once were the association
  members told that their slope may be given to the City.

  Christine Saracino, M.V.: expressed concern that the timeline is not being met for the
  construction at 26992 La Paja Lane. On May 18, 2009, the contractor promised that he
  could complete the project by September. She asked if the City is billing the homeowner
  for a full-time inspector and asked for an update from the City Attorney.

  Mayor Ury asked staff to provide the Council and residents with an update on the project
  before the end of the week.

  Robert David Breton, M.V.: thanked the City Council and staff for making tremendous
  strides with literacy and cultural arts in the community. He stated that the City’s Library
  programs are so important and during recessions, people appreciate free or low cost
  events more than ever. He also encouraged citizens of the community to contribute to the
  cultural landscape by uploading photos that depict “the spirit of thankfulness and caring”
  for display in the new Parkway Gallery.

  Linda DeFonce, M.V.: thanked the City Council for asking the Saddleback Valley
  Unified School District to stop any further action at the former O’Neill School site due to
  the lack of environmental studies. She stated that the District has repeatedly ignored the
  City’s requests and they are moving ahead with implementation of their plans at the site.
  She further noted that there were no crosswalks installed at De Portola Elementary and
  she expressed concern for the safety of the students attending that school.

PRESENTATIONS (Continued)

P2.  Proclaim September 26, 2009, as Mesothelioma Awareness Day in Mission Viejo

  Christa Ury and Aria Bendix, President of the Santa Margarita High School Breath of
  Hope Club, discussed Mesothelioma and thanked Mayor Ury for the proclamation.

City Council Minutes  4  September 8, 2009
 CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 20, 21, and 22 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve
the Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the Regular Meeting of July 20, 2009, as presented.

3.  Summary of FY 2009-10 Budget Amendments To Date

  Received and filed.

4.  City Treasurer's Monthly Report for June 2009

  Received and filed.

5.  Community Development Agency Treasurer's Monthly Report for June 2009

  Received and filed.

6.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer's Monthly Report for June 2009

  Received and filed.

City Council Minutes  5  September 8, 2009
 7.  Reduction in Community Development Agency (CDA) Outstanding Loan Balance

  Adopted (1) Resolution 09-35 Amending the FY 2009-10 Budget to Reflect a Payment
  of General Fund Loans by the Community Development Agency (CDA), and (2) CDA
  Resolution 09-05 Amending the FY 2009-10 Budget to Reflect a Payment of General
  Fund Loans.

8.  Check Register dated July 10, 2009, in the amount of $696,362.54

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

9.  Check Register dated July 17, 2009, in the amount of $834,204.88

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

10.  Check Register dated July 24, 2009, in the amount of $815,210.49

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

11.  Check Register dated July 31, 2009, in the amount of $1,300,039.15

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

12.  Check Register dated August 7, 2009, in the amount of $2,279,105.33

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

13.  Check Register dated August 14, 2009, in the amount of $913,827.07

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

14.  Check Register dated August 21, 2009, in the amount of $1,212,734.18

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

15.  Quarterly Check Register and Cash Receipts Reports – Fourth Quarter of FY 2008-
  09

  Received and filed.

City Council Minutes  6  September 8, 2009
 16.  Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo – For the Year Ended June 30, 2009
  (Preliminary-Unaudited)

  Received and filed.

17.  Financial Report for the Community Development Agency – For the Year Ended
  June 30, 2009 (Preliminary-Unaudited)

  Received and filed.

18.  Financial Reports for the Community Development Financing Authority – For the
  Year Ended June 30, 2009 (Preliminary-Unaudited)

  Received and filed.

19.  Review of 2008-2009 Orange County Grand Jury Report, "Paper Water - Does
  Orange County Have a Reliable Future?"

  Authorized the Mayor to send a letter to the Orange County Grand Jury commenting on
  the findings and recommendations cited in 2008-2009 Orange County Grand Jury Report,
  "Paper Water - Does Orange County Have a Reliable Future?"

23.  2009 Residential Resurfacing-Slurry Seal (CIP 838)

  Awarded the construction contract in the amount of $413,878.50 to Roy Allan Slurry
  Seal, Inc., for the subject project.

24.  Maintenance of Traffic Signals and Appurtenance

  Approved Contract Change Order 3 in the amount of $36,043.51 to Republic ITS and
  increase Purchase Order 090075.

25.  Oso Creek Restoration and Protection Project

  (1) Adopted Resolution 09-36 Amending the Fiscal Year 2009-10 Budget to Create
  Capital Improvement Project 207 to Construct the Oso Creek Restoration and Protection
  Project; (2) adopted Resolution 09-37 Authorizing the City Manager to Enter Into
  Agreements with the State Water Resources Control Board and Mission Viejo Country
  Club for the State Water Grant for the Oso Creek Restoration and Protection Project; and

City Council Minutes  7  September 8, 2009
   (3) authorized payment to the Mission Viejo Country Club following execution of the
  agreement with the Mission Viejo Country Club.

26.  2009 Residential Resurfacing - Slurry Seal (CIP 838) -- Medical Center Road
  Pavement Rehabilitation

  (1) Approved the bid specifications and authorized staff to advertise for construction bids
  for the subject project; and (2) adopted Resolution 09-38 Amending the Fiscal Year
  2009-2010 Budget for CIP 838.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

20.  Amendment to Schedule of Fines and Fees for the Mission Viejo Library

  Council Member Schlicht expressed opposition to the 100% increase for Saddleback
  Room set-up fees.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to
  adopt Library Resolution 09-01 Amending the Schedule of Fines and Fees for the
  Mission Viejo Library.

  Council Member Schlicht voiced concerns and asked if the Council could bifurcate the
  motion for room setup fees.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

21.  DCA2009-13 is an Ordinance Amending Section 9.10.020 of Article II of Title 9 of
  the Municipal Code Regarding Density Bonuses and Affordable Housing.
  DCA2009-14 is an Ordinance Amending Chapter 9.12 of Article II of Title 9 of the
  Municipal Code Regarding the Business Park / Industrial Zone to Allow for the By
  Right Construction of Emergency Shelters

City Council Minutes  8  September 8, 2009
   City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  Council Member Schlicht stated that she would be voting no for consistency with her
  July 20, 2009, vote on the same Ordinances.

  Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1) adopt
  Ordinance 09-275 Amending Section 9.10.020 of Article II of Title 9 of the Municipal
  Code Regarding Density Bonuses and Affordable Housing, and (2) adopt Ordinance 09-
  276 Amending Chapter 9.12 of Article II of Title 9 of the Municipal Code Regarding the
  Business Park / Industrial Zone to Allow for the By Right Construction of Emergency
  shelters.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

22.  Professional Services Agreement for Solid Waste and Recycling Consulting Services

  Senior Management Analyst Denise Matson presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to
  award the contract to SloanVazquez, LLC, in the amount of $94,660 for solid waste and
  recycling consulting services.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

27.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

28.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

City Council Minutes  9  September 8, 2009
   Mayor Pro Tem MacLean presented the report.

29.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Ledesma announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the San
  Joaquin Hills TCA.

30.  SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

31.  Presentation by Dr. Timothy McLarney of True North Research, Inc. Regarding
  Results of Customer Satisfaction Survey for Planning and Building Services
  Divisions in the Community Development Department

  Dr. Timothy McLarney presented a report on the results of the Customer Satisfaction
  Survey for the City's Planning and Building Services Divisions.

City Manager Wilberg drew the Council’s attention to the fall/winter edition of City Outlook
which features the First Annual Readers’ Festival on the cover. He announced that the Outlook
will arrive in residents’ mailboxes this week.

City Attorney’s Report

  City Attorney Bill Curley elaborated on the model landscaping ordinance that the Orange
  County Division of the League of California Cities is coordinating. The League is
  developing an ordinance that satisfies the State Law requirements but one that will allow
  local agencies to tailor the ordinance to its specific needs. The Ordinance will be coming
  to the City Council in the next few months and it must be acted-upon by the end of the
  year.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS

32.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities

City Council Minutes  10  September 8, 2009
   calendars as presented in the staff report and agreed to provide any changes to the City
  Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Kelley

  Council Member Kelley outlined her summer activities including her attendance at the
  very informative safety forum, National Night Out. She also discussed the successful
  blood drive she organized in honor of Mission Viejo’s hometown Marine, Alex Minsky,
  who was injured in Afghanistan. Council Member Kelley invited residents to two
  upcoming events: the first annual Readers’ Festival which will be held on Saturday,
  September 12, 2009, at the Norman P. Murray Community Center and the adjacent
  Village Green; and the Orange County International Triathlon which begins and ends at
  Lake Mission Viejo on September 27, 2009. She also reminded residents that
  information on all of the City’s events is available by subscription to the eNewsletter.
  Those interested can subscribe from the home page of the City’s web site to make sure
  they receive all of the City’s news and announcements. Council Member Kelley thanked
  her summer intern, Tina Segall, for volunteering her time and for her hard work on a
  variety of projects.

Council Member Ledesma

  Council Member Ledesma thanked Council Member Kelley for organizing the Alex
  Minsky blood drive. He stated that it was a tremendous effort on her part and on the part
  of the residents who participated.

Council Member Schlicht

  Council Member Schlicht announced that she too attended National Night Out. It was a
  tremendous program and she recalled Erin Runnion’s poignant story on the importance of
  child safety. Council Member Schlicht thanked the city's IT Department for assembling a
  great booklet of information entitled Practice Safe Computing. She encouraged residents
  to contact the City and obtain a copy. With flu season coming up, Council Member
  Schlicht inquired about getting automatic hand sanitizers installed in City facilities for the
  public’s use. She wished Happy New Year to the friends and neighbors who will be
  celebrating Rosh Hashanah in about ten days and Council Member Schlicht ended her
  comments by reading a written statement from resident Mark Dobrilovic, requesting
  action or clarification on the City’s room rental policy.

Mayor Pro Tem MacLean

City Council Minutes  11  September 8, 2009
   Mayor Pro Tem MacLean thanked the community and his colleagues for allowing him
  the opportunity to participate in the meeting remotely. He stated that this is a testimony
  to the technology we have today and he thanked Jackie Alexander and the IT staff for
  arranging the necessary equipment to allow him to be a full participating Council
  Member even though he is out of town. Mayor Pro Tem MacLean posted the Agenda on
  his hotel room door and he joked that he was disappointed that there were no members of
  the public there with him. He stated that it's been a nice summer break and we are getting
  back into the business of the City. He will be back in town for the next meeting and
  looks forward to seeing everyone then.

Mayor Ury

  Mayor Ury announced that the antibacterial liquids are already available at the City
  Recreation Centers and Council Member Schlicht has a good idea to install them at City
  Hall. He stated it went way too fast but he hopes everyone had an enjoyable summer.

ADJOURNMENT

  At the hour of 8:09 p.m., there being no further business to come before the City Council
  at this session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting to Monday, September 21, 2009, at
  5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of September 21, 2009

City Council Minutes  12  September 8, 2009
